strengths: The broad multilingual audit addresses an important NLP resource assumption. Separately reporting removal of 29.36% of documents and 11.68% of characters usefully demonstrates why article counts can misrepresent available training material.

Concrete examples of untranslated passages, placeholders, and repeated templates make the findings interpretable. The correlation between MinHash removal and independently estimated bot prevalence (ρ = 0.63) supports its usefulness for identifying redundant content.

The experimental coverage is substantial: 50-language monolingual pretraining, language adaptation, multilingual pretraining, and several downstream tasks. Article-count-matched random controls and five-run results for several experiments strengthen the empirical contribution. Some improvements are substantial, including Cebuano SIB200 accuracy increasing from 0.39 to 0.51.

The paper is generally well organized and provides extensive language-specific results, training hyperparameters, and a toolkit link. It also discusses adverse outcomes, particularly the large monolingual performance decrease for Acehnese.
weaknesses: The central quality interpretation exceeds the evidence. Filtering measures script mismatch and redundancy, but the conclusion labels approximately 30% of documents as low quality without systematic validation of retained and removed material. Appendix A explicitly removes foreign-script names and references, while templated articles can contain distinct useful facts. Preserved downstream accuracy establishes limited marginal utility for particular tasks, rather than validating a general quality judgment. Representative human evaluation or substantially narrower claims are needed.

The multilingual BELEBELE experiment cannot substantiate preservation of useful reading-comprehension ability: Table 14 reports average accuracy of 0.25 for both conditions, matching four-choice chance performance; even English scores are 0.25–0.26. The adaptation improvement from 0.25 to 0.30 is more encouraging, but lacks reported variability. These results need stronger evaluation diagnostics before supporting the claimed benefits across three practical scenarios.

The controls do not isolate the contribution of document selection. Random sampling matches article counts rather than token volume, although filtering disproportionately removes short articles. Appendix C also uses different tokenizers for raw and filtered training, while fixed-epoch monolingual and adaptation schedules entail different training budgets. These choices support practical pipeline comparisons, but common-tokenizer, token-budget-matched controls and representative filter ablations are needed for the stronger causal interpretation.

The four-tier taxonomy has limited independent validation. The DEPTH+ correlation of 0.31 provides modest corroboration, and correlations with bot prevalence or length-related heuristics do not establish general linguistic quality. The choice of four clusters and sensitivity to filtering thresholds are not examined. Moreover, treating differences within five percentage points as negligible does not establish equivalence; Table 13 shows average XNLI accuracy decreasing from 0.44 to 0.43.

Exact reproducibility remains uncertain from the manuscript: it omits a fixed Wikipedia snapshot, the text-extraction procedure, MinHash shingling and LSH configuration, and precise validation-split construction. The toolkit link and hyperparameter tables are helpful, but these omissions affect the central removal statistics and rankings. Together with the unresolved quality-label validation and chance-level evaluation, they prevent a clear Findings recommendation despite the useful descriptive contribution.
